public abstract class ResourceClientBase<M,J> extends ClientBase implements PageablePost<M>
Generic base for internal resource clients, collapsing the request-build → invoke → response-handle boilerplate that was previously copy-pasted across every *ClientImpl.

Parameterized over the public model type M and its JSON model J. The response TypeReference is derived from J (see RequestAssembler.deriveResponseType(RequestType, Class)), and the paging nextPage(...) methods are provided once here. Subclasses supply the JSON class and a wrap(Object) factory (which binds this client for refresh/paging) and then implement each operation as a one-line call to the protected helpers below, passing only the service-endpoint name.

Clients whose apiParams endpoint names follow the standard convention can additionally pass a resource name at construction and use the no-endpoint-name helper overloads: the default endpoint names are derived as List+plural, Search+plural, Get/ Create/Update/Delete+singular. Operations whose apiParams names deviate keep calling the explicit-name helpers.

public class ServiceProfileClientImpl extends ResourceClientBase<ServiceProfile, ServiceProfileJson>
        implements ServiceProfileClient<ServiceProfile> {
    public ServiceProfileClientImpl(FabricConfigImpl c) {
        super(c, "Fabric", "ServiceProfiles", ServiceProfileJson.class);
    }
    protected ServiceProfile wrap(ServiceProfileJson j) { return new ServiceProfileWrapper(j, this); }
    public Page<ServiceProfileJson> list()          { return listPage("ListServiceProfiles"); }
    public ServiceProfileJson getByUuid(String uuid) { return getOne("GetServiceProfile", uuid); }
    // ...
}

    • searchPageQueryPaginated

      protected Page<J> searchPageQueryPaginated(String serviceEndpoint, Object filterBody)
      POST search whose pagination travels as offset/limit query parameters (per the endpoint's spec) rather than inside the body — e.g. assets v1 and the EIA services/prices searches. Builds a PaginatedRequest (so the shared paging pipeline advances the query-parameter offset between pages, re-sending the same filter body) instead of a PaginatedPostRequest (whose paging advances state inside the body).

      Dry-run variant of patchOne(String, String, List): sends the identical RFC 6902 JSON Patch request (same application/json-patch+json content type) plus the dryRun=true query parameter — per the spec, an "option to verify that API calls will succeed".
